title: Three-Week IB French B Revision Plan
summary: IB French B revision plan for November: a flexible three-week schedule for topic triage, timed practice, listening, writing, and deliberate rest each day.
body_markdown:
Three weeks before an IB examination can feel both substantial and impossibly short. There is enough time to improve, but not enough time to relearn an entire language. The difference lies in choosing what deserves attention.


This **IB French B revision plan** is designed for November candidates who are also preparing for several other subjects. It uses focused sessions rather than marathon study days. Week one diagnoses weaknesses, week two develops exam skills, and week three rehearses performance under timed conditions. Rest is treated as part of the plan, not as time stolen from it.


The current Language B assessment model tests productive writing in Paper 1 and receptive listening and reading in Paper 2. Your preparation therefore needs to rotate between producing French, understanding French, and reviewing the language patterns connecting both.


### Your three-week plan at a glance


Week Main priority French workload


Week 1 Diagnose weaknesses and rebuild foundations 60-75 minutes on 5-6 days


Week 2 Practise writing, reading, and listening under pressure 75-90 minutes on 5-6 days


Week 3 Complete timed rehearsals and protect energy 45-90 minutes depending on the day


Keep one full evening free each week. If another subject has an examination first, shorten French sessions rather than abandoning them. Twenty focused minutes of listening or retrieval practice preserves momentum better than a guilty three-hour session that never happens.


A student negotiates a realistic daily revision plan with a towering pile of French books


### Week one: diagnose before you revise


The natural temptation is to begin with the topic you enjoy most. Diagnosis asks you to do the opposite. Before investing hours in vocabulary, determine whether marks are being lost through comprehension, limited expression, weak text conventions, poor timing, or avoidable misreading.


### Days 1-2: establish your baseline


Complete one representative writing task, one reading set, and one listening set. These do not need to be completed consecutively. Use the official time allowance shown on the current material, then mark or review your responses carefully.


Record errors under four headings:


- **Knowledge:** missing vocabulary or grammar
- **Comprehension:** misunderstanding a phrase, speaker, or question
- **Technique:** choosing the wrong text type or overlooking an instruction
- **Timing:** rushing, leaving gaps, or overinvesting in one section


This error log is more useful than a raw score. A score says what happened once. The categories suggest what you should do tomorrow.


The[IB French B Questionbank](https://www.revisiondojo.com/ib/ib-french-b/questionbank) lets you practise targeted exam-style questions without sitting a complete paper every day. If your baseline reveals a narrow weakness, such as inference in reading or selecting supporting details, isolate it there first.


### Days 3-6: triage topics and language


French B is organised around five broad themes: identities, experiences, human ingenuity, social organisation, and sharing the planet. Mark each theme red, amber, or green according to your ability to understand ideas and express an opinion about them.


For red topics, build a compact bank of useful language:


- 12-15 precise nouns and verbs
- 5 connective expressions
- 3 flexible examples
- 2 ways to express a qualified opinion
- 1 counterargument


Do not try to memorise a miniature dictionary. Vocabulary becomes valuable when you can retrieve and adapt it. Use[French B resources by level and topic](https://www.revisiondojo.com/ib/ib-french-b) alongside Study Notes and Flashcards, then test yourself without looking.


Finish week one with a second short diagnostic. If an error persists, keep it on next week's priority list. If it disappears, move forward.


### Week two: turn knowledge into exam performance


Week one asks, “What do I know?” Week two asks, “Can I use it when the clock is running?” This is where IB French B revision becomes less comfortable and more productive.


### Build a repeatable writing process


Complete three writing tasks across the week. Give each session a different purpose:


1. One untimed task focused on accuracy and organisation.
2. One partially timed task focused on planning and text conventions.
3. One fully timed task completed without notes.


Before writing, identify the audience, purpose, context, required content, and suitable text type. Then create a brief plan. A reliable structure with clear development is usually safer than complicated French you cannot control.


Afterward, use RevisionDojo's Grading tools or AI Chat to identify recurring issues, but verify suggestions against your course materials and teacher guidance. Convert corrections into rules. For example, do not merely rewrite a mistaken adjective agreement. Add a reminder explaining why the form changes and produce two fresh examples.


For a wider strategy,[How to Get a 7 in IB French B](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/how-to-get-a-7-in-ib-french-b) explains how language accuracy, task fulfilment, and regular skill practice fit together.


### Alternate reading and listening


On non-writing days, alternate receptive skills:


- **Reading day:** predict the text's purpose, scan the questions, locate evidence, and review why distractors were wrong.
- **Listening day:** anticipate likely vocabulary, note changes in speaker attitude, and distinguish the main message from supporting detail.


Listening improves through repeated, purposeful exposure. On the first listen, follow meaning. On the second, identify evidence. On the third, study the phrases that prevented understanding. Passive audio playing in the background may provide exposure, but it is not a substitute for answering questions and reviewing mistakes.


The guide to[French B resources for self-study](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/best-ib-french-b-resources-self-study) can help you combine structured IB practice with authentic French listening and reading.


### Keep the plan compatible with other subjects


Use three session lengths:


- **20 minutes:** Flashcards, error-log review, or focused listening
- **45 minutes:** one skill set followed by correction
- **90 minutes:** a complete timed section and detailed review


Choose according to the rest of your examination calendar. The plan succeeds through continuity, not identical days.


### Week three: rehearse, refine, and recover


The final week is not the moment to collect ten new resources. It is the moment to make familiar processes dependable.


### Sit timed papers in Exam mode


Complete two substantial timed rehearsals during the week. Use RevisionDojo Predicted Papers or Mock Exams in **Exam mode** , with your phone away and only the materials permitted in the real assessment. Match the official timings printed on the current paper you are using.


After each rehearsal, spend at least as long reviewing as you spent checking the final score. Return to the[French B Questionbank](https://www.revisiondojo.com/ib/ib-french-b/questionbank) for targeted repair between simulations. A complete paper reveals the weakness; focused practice changes it.


A useful rhythm is:


- **Days 15-16:** timed Paper 1 rehearsal, review, and one rewritten section
- **Days 17-18:** timed Paper 2 reading and listening practice, followed by error analysis
- **Day 19:** mixed Questionbank practice on the two weakest areas
- **Day 20:** light retrieval, text-type review, and listening warm-up
- **Day 21:** rest, organise materials, and stop early


If two examinations fall close together, split a rehearsal across separate days. Conditions should still be quiet and timed, even when the sections are separated.


### Protect the marks you already have


In the final 48 hours, reduce volume. Review your red-flag grammar list, common instructions, text conventions, and flexible thematic vocabulary. Keep French in your ear through a short audio segment, but avoid exhausting full simulations.


Sleep is not a reward for finishing revision. It supports attention, recall, and judgement, which are precisely the abilities needed when a listening answer appears once and the next question is already approaching.


### A calm finish is still a serious finish


Three weeks will not make every French sentence effortless. It can, however, make your preparation far more deliberate. You can know which topics need attention, recognise your recurring errors, and enter the examination with a process you have already rehearsed.


RevisionDojo brings that process into one place. Study Notes and Flashcards rebuild knowledge, AI Chat and Grading tools support correction, and the Questionbank turns weaknesses into focused practice. Predicted Papers and Mock Exams then let you test the whole system under timed conditions. If a persistent gap needs personal explanation, RevisionDojo Tutors can provide additional guidance, while the Coursework Library remains useful for broader IB support outside this final examination sprint.


Start with one diagnostic, not an ambitious promise. Then[practise French B questions by topic](https://www.revisiondojo.com/ib/ib-french-b/questionbank) and sit your timed papers in Exam mode. The calendar becomes less intimidating once every day has a clear job.
